title: Diwali Comes to Montana's Governor's Mansion for the First Time
excerpt: Governor Greg Gianforte hosted the festival in Helena on October 26, in a consulate-led season of Diwali firsts across the American north-west — complete with a 'London Thumakda' dance floor.
body:
• Diwali was celebrated at the Montana Governor's Mansion in Helena for the first time, hosted by Governor Greg Gianforte and First Lady Susan Gianforte on October 26.
  • The celebration was organised by the Consulate General of India in Seattle with the Montana World Affairs Council, as part of the consulate's Diwali events across the northwestern states.
  • Guests danced to the Bollywood track 'London Thumakda' — the moment from the evening that travelled furthest online.
  • Washington cities Kent, Tacoma and Lynnwood also issued Diwali proclamations this season, and North Dakota held its own first governor's-residence Diwali on October 29.

Diwali has reached one of the last statehouses in America where it had never been celebrated. Governor Greg Gianforte and First Lady Susan Gianforte hosted the festival at the Governor's Mansion in Helena on October 26 — the first Diwali celebration at the Montana mansion — according to ANI's report of the event. The detail that travelled furthest was the dancing: Montanans dancing to 'London Thumakda', the exuberant Bollywood wedding track, in the governor's residence.

Part of a consulate-wide Diwali season

The Helena celebration was organised by the Consulate General of India in Seattle with the Montana World Affairs Council. The Seattle consulate's jurisdiction covers Idaho, Nebraska, Montana, North Dakota, Washington and Oregon, and this season it ran Diwali celebrations across that whole arc — including city hall events in Washington, where Kent, Tacoma and Lynnwood issued Diwali proclamations. Three days after Helena, on October 29, North Dakota Governor Kelly Armstrong and First Lady Kjersti Armstrong hosted that state's first Diwali at the Governor's Residence in Bismarck, with families travelling in from Fargo, Grand Forks and across the state for the ceremonial lighting of the diya.

Why these firsts matter

Montana's Indian-American community is small compared with the diaspora's coastal centres, which is precisely what makes a governor's-mansion Diwali significant there: official recognition does not follow population size alone. Across the US this Diwali season, the pattern has repeated — statehouses, city halls and school districts marking a festival that a generation ago was celebrated almost entirely in homes and temples. For Montana's Indian families, the October 26 celebration puts Diwali on the state's civic calendar alongside its other communities' festivals — and gives the Montana World Affairs Council, which also runs the state's India student-exchange links with Helena, a cultural anchor for the relationship it has been building with the Seattle consulate.

The wider season

The north-western firsts land in a year when Diwali's civic footprint in the US keeps widening — from California's new (and legally contested) Diwali school-holiday law to fireworks-permit warnings in Edmonton and drive-through celebrations in New Jersey townships. The Helena evening was smaller than any of those. Its claim is simpler: for the first time, the Festival of Lights was lit at Montana's Governor's Mansion, and the governor danced to Bollywood.
